title: Reframe — What You Would Do Differently

timed_text.text: We did a reframe exercise earlier in the series.
You've added tools — reset word, If-Then plan, self-talk replacements.
Your mistake protocol, the fighter mindset, your focus anchors trained.
I want you to go back to a different moment.
One you've carried as a failure — where your mind got in the way.
Not to relive the pain, but to rewrite the response.
You're not pretending the bad moment didn't happen.
You're showing your nervous system: there's a trained answer now.
Every time you do this, that memory loses its charge.
Next time it arrives, your brain looks for the trained response.
Think of a moment that still stings a little.
On your screen, you're going to walk through it.

cards.prompt: Describe the moment — the situation, what happened, what your mind did, and how it affected your performance.
At what exact point did the spiral begin? What was the trigger thought?
Replay it with your full toolkit. From that exact moment — walk through what you would have done. Every step. Reset word, physical cue, focus anchor, self-talk replacement. Be specific.
Read your reframed response back. This is your trained answer to that moment now.

timed_text.text: That memory just became a rep. You've already been there with a plan.
Next, you've got a journal and after you finish, day 26 is complete.

blocks.prompt: How did it feel to give your brain a trained response for that moment? Did the weight of that memory change at all?
